title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 44
paragraphs: These were the Peloponnesians who joined the fleet. Those from the mainland outside the Peloponnese were as follows. The Athenians, furnishing a larger number than all the rest combined — namely, 180 ships — and serving alone, since the Plataeans did not take part with the Athenians in the sea-fight at Salamis: for when the Greeks were leaving Artemisium and were near Chalkis, the Plataeans disembarked on the opposite shore of Boeotia and began removing their households. Being engaged in saving these, they were left behind. As for the Athenians, in the days when the Pelasgians inhabited what is now called Greece, they were Pelasgians and were called Cranaoi; in the time of King Kecrops they came to be called Kecropidai; when Erechtheus succeeded to power, they had their name changed to Athenians; and after Ion son of Xuthos became commander of the Athenians, they got from him the name of Ionians.
